title: PakBBQ: A Culturally Adapted Bias Benchmark for QA
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured stereotypical biases related to religion, specifically focusing on sectarian affiliations (e.g., Barelvi, Deobandi within Islam) and biases towards minority religious groups (e.g., Christians, Hindus, Ahmadis) within the Pakistani sociocultural context.
findings: Models struggled with culturally specific religious contexts unique to Pakistan, showing the lowest accuracy on 'Newly Added' templates that included sectarian and religious minority biases. However, models also demonstrated strong counter-bias tendencies, particularly in the religion category when contexts were unambiguous. On average, models showed greater counter-bias in Urdu compared to English.
references: Noreen Abbas. 2018. Address forms and gender in urdu: A sociolinguistic perspective. Journal of Arts and Linguistics Studies, 2(1):94–104.
